name: starter role library
description: Roles installed with a new tenant, and the deployment's own platform roles. Data, not code: a role is a tenant-authored set of permissions (critique-log defect #7), so even the ones NEMESIS ships are a starting point a customer edits by copying. Permission strings are declared in nemesis/identity/permissions.py and validated on write; a typo here fails provisioning rather than producing a role that silently permits nothing.

platform.name: Platform support
platform.description: Reads a customer's console through an audited, time-capped impersonation session. Holds no customer permission of its own: everything it can see, it sees as the user it is acting as, and every decision is recorded against the operator's subject.

platform.name: Platform administrator
platform.description: Provisions tenants and reads the deployment's integrity findings. Deliberately does not carry impersonation:start — onboarding a customer and reading their screen are different jobs, and an operator who needs both holds two roles so the audit says which one they were using.

tenant.name: Administrator
tenant.description: Configures the tenant and administers access. Does not carry review:decide: judging a flagged citizen report is operational work on a person's complaint, and an administrator who happens to hold the keys is not automatically the right person to do it. Grant both where one person genuinely does both jobs.

tenant.name: Department head
tenant.description: Runs one department's queue. Granted on a department scope, never tenant-wide — the Phase 13 gate clause is that department head A cannot read department B's rows, and a tenant-wide grant of this role is how that stops being true.

tenant.name: Zone officer
tenant.description: Covers everything happening in one part of the city, across departments. Granted on a zone scope. Named for the place tree rather than for a municipal job title, because the same role is a ward officer in a city, a campus warden on a university, and an estate manager in an industrial park.

tenant.name: Field staff
tenant.description: Sees only what they are personally attached to. Granted on the 'self' scope, which is a relationship rather than a place: the rows are defined by who holds the grant, which is why it cannot be delegated.

tenant.name: Trust & safety reviewer
tenant.description: Works the Phase 8 human review queue and nothing else. The narrowest useful role in the library, and the one worth copying when composing a new one: it holds the two permissions its job needs and no read of the control plane at all.

tenant.name: Contractor lead
tenant.description: A contractor organisation's own administrator. Granted on a contractor scope, which restricts it to that organisation's rows. Carries no reporter-contact permission: a contractor repairing a road does not need the citizen's phone number, and §22 treats that as a different disclosure from the photograph of the pothole.

tenant.name: Analyst
tenant.description: Reads everything the tenant publishes about itself and the evidence behind a policy, and changes nothing. The role to hand an auditor, a journalist under an agreement, or a councillor's office.
